summary_hint: Tells a processor which property, who did the work, when it was finished, and whether the property cleared.

typed_core.name: document_title
typed_core.why: identity — confirms this is a completion/clearance vs an inspection report

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity/source — issuing organization (often the pest-control company)

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity — the subject property the clearance attaches to (degraded from address)

typed_core.name: owner_buyer_or_builder_name
typed_core.why: identity — owner/buyer named on the certificate; match to borrower/seller (flattened from person_or_entity[])

typed_core.name: owner_buyer_or_builder_name_2
typed_core.why: identity — second named party (co-owner/co-buyer)

typed_core.name: pest_control_or_treatment_company
typed_core.why: identity/source — the licensed company performing the work (degraded from entity)

typed_core.name: company_license_number
typed_core.why: processor — company licensure, so the certificate can be trusted

typed_core.name: technician_or_applicator_name
typed_core.why: processor — applicator identity (degraded/flattened from object)

typed_core.name: technician_or_applicator_license
typed_core.why: processor — applicator license number

typed_core.name: original_inspection_report_date
typed_core.why: disambiguator — ties the completion to the report whose findings it clears

typed_core.name: original_inspection_report_number
typed_core.why: disambiguator — the report number being cleared

typed_core.name: completion_date
typed_core.why: processor — headline: when the work was finished (recency/validity through closing)

typed_core.name: areas_or_structures_treated
typed_core.why: processor — what was treated (degraded/joined from string[])

typed_core.name: warranty_or_guarantee_terms
typed_core.why: processor — warranty/guarantee offered on the work

typed_core.name: clearance_or_no_remaining_evidence_statement
typed_core.why: processor — headline: the clearance/no-remaining-evidence statement
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the clearance/no-remaining-evidence statement verbatim; a completion can be full or partial (Section 1 vs Section 2 items)

typed_core.name: follow_up_inspection_required
typed_core.why: processor — whether a re-inspection is still outstanding (degraded from bool)
typed_core.prompt_hint: true means the file is not yet fully cleared even though work was done

typed_core.name: invoice_amount
typed_core.why: processor — cost of the work (flattened from invoice object)

typed_core.name: invoice_paid_status
typed_core.why: processor — whether the work is paid (who owes at closing)
typed_core.prompt_hint: Invoice paid status matters for who bears the cost at closing — record amount and paid/unpaid as stated

typed_core.name: company_representative_name
typed_core.why: execution — the signer certifying completion (flattened from signature)

typed_core.name: company_representative_signed_date
typed_core.why: execution — when completion was certified

nested_lists.name: treatment_or_repair_items_completed
nested_lists.shape_reason: the itemized work done repeats (a handful to ~20 items); flat rows with one source each are token-safe and let a processor see line-by-line what was completed

fields.name: method_or_chemical
fields.why: processor — treatment method / chemical used (brand or active ingredient)

fields.name: area
fields.why: processor — the area the item was completed in

fields.name: status
fields.why: processor — completion status of the item

rejected.name: form_number, form_revision_date
rejected.reason: state forms are inconsistently numbered; document_title suffices

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start/_end
rejected.reason: not applicable; completion_date is the operative date

rejected.name: loan_number, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: rarely on a WDO completion; leave to catch-all

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: single rep signature covers execution; not notarized/versioned

rejected.name: treatment_method_and_chemical (separate object[])
rejected.reason: folded into the one nested item list to stay within the one-list budget

rejected.name: contractor_repair_details (separate object[])
rejected.reason: folded into the nested item list; a second list is not justified by any rule

rejected.name: owner_builder_or_buyer_acknowledgment
rejected.reason: rarely present; captured in catch-all if it appears

encoding_variations: Titles vary by state form ('Notice of Completion', 'Wood Destroying Pest Completion', NPMA/state clearance forms); rely on content, not title

'Clearance' may be an explicit clearance statement, a 'Section 1 cleared' notation, or a 'no remaining evidence' sentence — capture the statement verbatim; do not reduce to a boolean, because partial clearances exist
Treatment chemicals may be named by brand or active ingredient — captured inside the nested item list
Original inspection reference may appear as a date, a report number, or both — both fields carry it so the completion can be matched to its report

open_questions.q: Which repeating list to keep. The catalog splits completed work across treatment_or_repair_items_completed, treatment_method_and_chemical, and contractor_repair_details.
options: one consolidated treatment_or_repair_items_completed flat-row list carrying method/chemical and area as columns
open_questions.recommendation: one consolidated flat-row list; confirm this consolidation is acceptable vs three separate lists

open_questions.q: areas_or_structures_treated flattened to str, joined into one string rather than a second list.
open_questions.recommendation: joined str, since it is short and the item list already carries per-item area; flag if a queryable structure list is wanted

open_questions.q: Clearance as verbatim str vs boolean.
open_questions.recommendation: kept verbatim because partial clearances exist; confirm no downstream consumer expects a clean pass/fail flag (which would misread partials)

notes: A completion certifies that previously-called-out work was done, distinct from the inspection report that called it out (packet 097).

No PII requiring registration — company and applicator license numbers are business identifiers, not personal PII; owner_buyer_or_builder_name is a personal name kept typed for identity, not a registry element.

Ambiguity: company_representative_name and company_representative_signed_date are tagged 'execution' in the markdown, which is not one of the five reason classes; both mapped to reason_class 'processor' (execution status is a processor-facing verification concern).
